ticket.title: users.ts:933 answers success: true over a 0-row profile update — KS-943 changes the symptom from stale values to undefined ones
ticket.description:
# KS-1050 — Wednesday's task for Ornith (written from the ticket AND the code at develop M55 `48e65c435`, 2026-09-15 11:1x–11:2x — the header clocks were first TYPED as 12:xx and corrected from `date` at 11:29)

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
In `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`, the `PATCH /me` profile-update handler (lines 918–952) calls
`userRepo.updateUser(user.id, updates)` at line 933 and then answers `success: true` unconditionally (line 937),
using `updated?.id` etc. Since KS-943, `updateUser` returns `null` when its UPDATE matched 0 rows (fail-closed RLS
with an unresolved tenant GUC). So a write that never landed is reported to the caller as a successful profile update
with `undefined` fields. The wallet routes already check this return (`routes/wallet.ts:488-495`) and throw an
`AppError(..., 500, 'WALLET_LINK_NOT_PERSISTED')`; this handler does the same, with its own code. (Wednesday's
reading of the ticket's "a 5xx like the wallet paths now do" — the in-file precedent — chosen for consistency.)

## The exact change — TWO SMALL EDITS, each its own hunk with 3 lines of context
(Keep every line not named below byte-identical, including indentation. No rewrite of the handler.)

E1 — line 16: `import { BadRequestError, NotFoundError, ValidationError } from '../middleware/errorHandler';` becomes
```
import { AppError, BadRequestError, NotFoundError, ValidationError } from '../middleware/errorHandler';
```
E2 — after line 933 `    const updated = await userRepo.updateUser(user.id, updates);` insert these FOUR lines
(before the existing line 934 `    logger.info('User profile updated', { userId: user.id });`):
```
    // KS-1050: a 0-row UPDATE answers null since KS-943 — never report success over it.
    if (!updated) {
      throw new AppError('Profile update did not persist — the update matched no row', 500, 'PROFILE_UPDATE_NOT_PERSISTED');
    }
```
Nothing else changes: the `updates` construction (924–931), the `res.json` block (936–948), the catch. The result:
a null return throws a 500 `PROFILE_UPDATE_NOT_PERSISTED` through `errorHandler`; a real row still answers 200.
You MAY also drop the now-unneeded `?.` in lines 939–946 — but do not; leave them byte-identical (smaller diff).

## The test — one new vitest file, in-process, no server beyond the one the reference test builds
File: `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1050-profile-update-zero-rows-is-not-success.test.ts`
Copy the mocking shape from `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1013-admin-patch-malformed-id.test.ts` (it hoists a
`repoMock` with `vi.hoisted`, mocks `../repositories/userRepo`, `../middleware/authenticate` (injects `req.user`),
`../db`, `../services/session`, `../services/password`, `../utils/logger`; mounts `userRoutes` + `errorHandler` on
an express app listening on 127.0.0.1:0; calls it with `fetch`). Seed `state.users` with the caller's own id as a
USER with `tenantId: 'tenant-default'` so `getUserById` finds it; the caller is `{ userId: <that id>, role: 'USER',
tenantId: 'tenant-default' }`. **COPY THIS hoisted block EXACTLY (the 11:28 AND 12:1x attempts both declared `const SEED_USER_ID` above it and read it inside — a TDZ, the file never loads):
```
const state = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  caller: { userId: 'aaaaaaaa-2222-4222-8222-aaaaaaaaaaaa', role: 'USER', tenantId: 'tenant-default' },
  users: new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>(),
}));
const SEED_USER_ID = 'aaaaaaaa-2222-4222-8222-aaaaaaaaaaaa'; // declared AFTER the hoisted block, used only in beforeEach/cells
```
**Inside `vi.hoisted(() => ({ … }))` write the id as a STRING LITERAL — never a `const`
declared elsewhere in the file: the hoisted block runs before every declaration, so a `const SEED_USER_ID` read inside
it throws `Cannot access 'SEED_USER_ID' before initialization` and the file never loads (the 11:28 attempt).** `PATCH /me` with body `{ firstName: 'Ada' }`. Cells:
- 🔴 `it('🔴 KS-1050 — updateUser returns null: the response is NOT success 200')`: `repoMock.updateUser`
  resolves `null`; assert `res.status` is 500 and the JSON body has `success: false` and error code
  `'PROFILE_UPDATE_NOT_PERSISTED'`. (Untouched code: 200 `success: true` — the red.)
- 🔴 `it('🔴 KS-1050 — a null return never answers success: true')`: same stub; assert the body's `success` is not
  `true`. (Untouched code: `true` — the red.)
- CONTROL `it('KS-1050 control — updateUser returns the row: 200 success with the row values')`:
  `repoMock.updateUser` resolves `{ ...seeded user, firstName: 'Ada', updatedAt: new Date() }`; assert 200,
  `success: true`, `data.firstName === 'Ada'` — before and after.

## Where (parsed into the checklist — every **must change** line must appear as a `-` line in your diff)
* `:16` — **must change**: `import { BadRequestError, NotFoundError, ValidationError } from '../middleware/errorHandler';`
* `:933` — (correct) `    const updated = await userRepo.updateUser(user.id, updates);` — stays; the guard goes right after it
* `:934` — (correct) `    logger.info('User profile updated', { userId: user.id });` — stays byte-identical; the four
  inserted lines go BETWEEN :933 and :934 (show :933 and :934 as context lines around the `+` lines)

## Output
Exactly ONE ```diff block; paths repo-relative (`Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/...`); correct hunk counts; blank
context lines keep their leading space; the product hunks stay inside lines 14–18 and 930–937.
